did_you_know.text: Did you know that the "Plains of Moab" was the last place the Israelites encamped before entering the Land of Israel? It's a significant geographical marker.

Did you know that the phrase "across the Jordan near Jericho" specifies the location of the Plains of Moab on the eastern side of the Jordan, opposite the city of Jericho on the western side? It highlights their physical proximity to the Promised Land.
Did you know that the name "Balak" is related to the Hebrew word "balak," meaning emptiness or devastation, perhaps hinting at his character as a king who wished to destroy Israel?
Did you know that Moab and Midian were usually in conflict, but now they unite to face the common threat from the Israelites? This demonstrates the severity of their fear.
Did you know that "Pethor, which is by the river" often refers to the Euphrates River, indicating that Balaam was a renowned sorcerer from a great distance?

Did you know that Balak sent for Balaam out of a strong belief in his power, as he stated: "for I know that whomever you bless is blessed, and whomever you curse is cursed"? This shows the reputation Balaam had.

Did you know that the phrase "with the fees for divination in their hand" implies that Balak's messengers brought money or gifts for Balaam, as was customary in ancient times for services of prophecy and cursing?

Did you know that even though Balaam declared, "If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the Lord my God," he still tried to persuade God, revealing his greed?
Did you know that God was angry with Balaam even though He gave him permission to go? The anger was due to Balaam's intent – he wanted to go to get rich and curse, not to obey God.
Did you know that the donkey saw the angel before Balaam did? This highlights that animals sometimes perceive supernatural or spiritual phenomena before humans do.
Did you know that the talking donkey is one of the most famous stories in the Bible, demonstrating a unique miracle where God uses creation to communicate with humans?

Did you know that the donkey emphasized her consistent loyalty to Balaam and that she had never accustomed herself to misbehaving? This made Balaam realize there had to be a supernatural reason for her actions.

Did you know that the angel of the Lord said, "Behold, I have come out to be an adversary [satan]," where "satan" here means an opponent or impediment, not necessarily the devil as commonly understood?
Did you know that "Bamoth Baal" (the high places of Baal) were pagan worship sites dedicated to the god Baal? Balak took Balaam to such a place, believing he would be able to curse Israel from there.
